rows.evidence: Q1: Conditions, materials and methods / Results and Discussion - three-year (2013-2015) field experiments at KazNIIZiR demonstration plots on light-chestnut soil with furrow control, surface and subsurface drip with and without mulch film; weed counts, biomass and yield (Tables 2-4) reported as own data.
rows.notes: The study's own weed result is attributed to the mulch film, not to drip irrigation: weed counts were 18-23 plants/m2 in mulch-film options and up to 165 plants/m2 in options without mulch film, which include the surface and subsurface drip treatments without film as well as the furrow control; the conclusion states that cultivation under mulch film at drip irrigation reduces weed infestation 8-10 times versus control. There is no reported comparison showing drip alone (without mulch) reduced weeds relative to furrow irrigation, so the passage's attribution of the 8-10-fold reduction to drip versus surface irrigation is not supported by the study's own evidence. Weed counts are reported only as ranges without replication statistics; no limitations stated.

notes: Text appears complete. Weed infestation data are given only in the text as ranges (no table); the 8-10x reduction is a mulch-film effect under drip, stated in the Conclusion.
